column1: # mapping_set_description: Proposed mapping of the columns of apply_qpcr_samples.csv to FAIRe terms (FAIRe_checklist_v1.0.2.xlsx)
# comment: each row's comment says what the FAIRe term means, why it was proposed, what the
#   apply mapping tool will do with the values and, for rows to review, what to check.
#   combine_order numbers the columns that together build one value, in order
#   (geo_loc_name is country, then region, then locality). value_part says which part of each
#   cell a term takes: number or unit (1 L fills samp_size and samp_size_unit), latitude or
#   longitude (MIxS lat_lon), or a conversion (negative control if yes). The apply mapping
#   tool applies rows with skos:exactMatch; change a row to skos:exactMatch to confirm it.
#   A column with no skos:exactMatch row is kept as a user-defined field, unless the apply
#   mapping tool is set to leave such columns out. Rows with a MIxS or Darwin Core term (MIXS: or
#   dwc:) are for columns with no FAIRe term: confirmed, they name the user-defined field.

column8: FAIRe term: samp_name. Sample Name is a name that you choose for the sample. Why: Strong match. The column name matches 'sample identifier', another name for this FAIRe term. A different value on every row. For example: W1, W2, W3.

FAIRe term: samp_category. A type/category of a sample. Allowed values: sample, negative control, positive control, PCR standard. Why: Moderate match. The column name partly matches the FAIRe term's own name ('sample category'). Values match the allowed values (100% of distinct values).

FAIRe term: neg_cont_type. A negative control type used in an investigation. Allowed values: site negative, field negative, process negative, extraction negative, PCR negative. Why: Strong match. The column name matches the FAIRe term's own name ('negative control type'). Values match the allowed values (100% of distinct values).

FAIRe term: eventDate. The date and time of sampling, either as an instance (single point in time) or interval. Why: Strong match. The column name matches 'date', another name for this FAIRe term. Dates (dd/mm/yyyy). What happens: The tool will convert dates from dd/mm/yyyy to ISO 8601 (yyyy-mm-dd).

FAIRe term: decimalLatitude. The geographic latitude in decimal degrees using WGS84 datum. Why: Strong match. The column name matches 'latitude', another name for this FAIRe term. Values are decimal degrees within latitude range (-42.9302 to -42.8901).

FAIRe term: decimalLongitude. The geographic longitude in decimal degrees using WGS84 datum. Why: Strong match. The column name matches 'longitude', another name for this FAIRe term. Values are decimal degrees within longitude range (147.33 to 147.38).

FAIRe term: geo_loc_name. The geographical origin of the sample as defined by the country or sea name followed by regions and localities. Why: Strong match. The column name matches 'country', another name for this FAIRe term. Country or sea names, the first part of "Country: region, locality". For example: Australia.

FAIRe term: env_broad_scale. Major environmental system your sample came from. Why: Strong match. The column name matches the FAIRe term's own name ('environment broad scale'). Values are in "label [ID]" form (e.g. ENVO terms).

FAIRe term: env_local_scale. The entity or entities which are in your sample or specimen’s local vicinity and which you believe have significant causal influences on your sample. Why: Strong match. The column name matches the FAIRe term's own name ('environment local scale'). Values are in "label [ID]" form (e.g. ENVO terms).

FAIRe term: env_medium. Environmental material or materials (pipe separated) immediately surrounded your sample prior to sampling. Why: Strong match. The column name matches the FAIRe term's own name ('environment medium'). Values are in "label [ID]" form (e.g. ENVO terms).
